##  · DOC1-agent-harness — userland/agents.md: the agent harness (Redoubt.Agent)

Status: **resolved** · Assigned to: Orchestrator · Revision: 6

Decision references: docs/userland/agents.md#the-agent-harness, docs/userland/agents.md#no-credentials-in-agent-memory

Evidence: docs/userland/agents.md: no pause or resume, lease and connections from the steward, loop in the agent's VM, no distribution or binary_to_term, no keys until M5; Open: none.

### Userland writer · Question

Event: `a46efd48614245727796df52aac49003` · 2026-09-26T08:01:42Z

> M4 (self-hosted development): 'the agent harness gives agents capabilities narrowed from their launcher's'. The draft: `Redoubt.Agent.start(model:, lease:, labels:, workspace:, tools:)` runs the harness in the launcher's VM and the agent in its own beamlet VM under a lease; tools are capabilities (a file connection, a gateway connection, a sub-budget to launch in); `prompt`, `status`, `kill` (destroy the lease); `pause`/`resume` 'if supported'. Undecided: (a) pause/resume: no kernel call freezes a budget; (b) who asks the steward for the lease; (c) whether the model loop runs in the agent's VM or the harness. RECOMMENDATION: (a) drop pause/resume (no freeze exists; a weight-0 budget is not a freeze); (b) the harness asks the steward, which makes the lease under the sponsor and mints fresh connections for each tool; (c) the loop runs in the agent's VM, talking to the model through its own gatewayd connection, so the launcher's VM never parses model output. Until answered the page lists these under Open.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `ffc66bf4bebc25618140bb4c8cee0aec` · 2026-09-26T08:05:26Z

> Architect ruling, userland/agents.md, M4 (self-hosted development). All three recommendations are adopted, with the settled rules they rest on and four additions. Nothing stays Open.
> 
> (a) DROP pause/resume. There is no freeze, and none can be emulated. R7 (carving) refuses a carve that leaves a budget holding a process with free weight 0, so 'weight 0' is not even reachable. A lease's kernel deadline keeps running regardless, so a pause would silently eat lease time. If someone wants a freeze later, it is a kernel feature for beyond/, not a harness call.
> 
> (b) The harness asks, and the steward makes the lease. This is settled by the agent rules (legacy CAPABILITIES, Agents):
> - An agent is its own principal, never an impersonation. So its connections must carry the agent's own badge, minted fresh by the steward for each tool. The harness cannot hand over its own connections, because every request made through them would be attributed to the sponsor.
> - The steward places the lease under the sponsor's budget for that label set. It checks that each tool is the same as or narrower than what the launcher holds, and that the lease is at most MAX_LEASE (24 h), refusing longer rather than clamping. It audits the grant with the principal chain.
> - No approval is needed while everything narrows. A label the launcher lacks (an agent that must read secrets) or a durable principal goes through the powerbox approval, as settled.
> - Sub-agents: an agent's harness asks the steward the same way, through its own powerbox connection. The sub-lease sits inside the agent's budget, so it ends with it (R10 (destruction)).
> 
> (c) The model loop runs in the agent's VM, through the agent's own gatewayd connection. That connection is scoped to the provider the launcher's own gateway grant allows, and gatewayd keeps the API key. The launcher's VM never parses model output.
> 
> ADDITIONS:
> 1. The harness-agent link is a typed Redoubt channel, never Erlang distribution. Distribution would give each VM full RPC into the other. What the harness receives (prompt replies, status) is untrusted data. It is decoded with a bounded decoder that creates no atoms and no code, and never with binary_to_term. So even Agent.prompt's reply cannot reach into the launcher's VM.
> 2. kill and status go through the steward, not a budget handle held in the launcher's VM. 'Ending a lease is always accepted from the sponsor, ahead of admission' (settled), and kill is audited. The launcher never holds the lease's budget handle, so it cannot create processes inside the agent's budget and blur attribution.
> 3. The agent never gets the sponsor's /dev/cons, keys (except from M5 (persist, install, share) onward, a key named in its approval, with one message shape) or a budget handle beyond its own. This restates the settled rules; the page cites them.
> 4. The page's API table drops pause and resume. start's options map one-to-one onto the steward's lease request: pages, processes, weight, time, labels, and a list of tools, each a narrowed grant.
> 
> TESTS, in M4's attack suite:
> - an agent's tool request broader than its launcher's is refused;
> - a lease over MAX_LEASE is refused;
> - the agent's requests to fsd and gatewayd carry the agent's badge, not the sponsor's;
> - a hostile reply to Agent.prompt (a malformed term or an atom flood) cannot crash or run code in the harness;
> - a kill ends every sub-agent;
> - the harness holds no handle to the lease's budget.

### Architect · Progress

Event: `c45a094e05e932a7df6a105da302a4db` · 2026-09-26T08:05:26Z

> cc: DOC1-agent-harness answered. All three recommendations are adopted, and nothing stays Open.
> (a) pause/resume are dropped: R7 refuses weight 0 with a process, and the deadline keeps running.
> (b) The steward makes the lease and mints fresh agent-badged connections for each tool. This is settled by 'own principal, never an impersonation'. Narrowing needs no approval; a new label does.
> (c) The loop runs in the agent's VM through its own gatewayd connection.
> Additions: the harness-agent link is typed IPC, never Erlang distribution, and replies are untrusted with no binary_to_term; kill and status go through the steward, so the launcher never holds the lease budget handle; the API table drops pause and resume.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `30b031ae9c9eb782272c53cc0f15da30` · 2026-09-26T08:05:35Z

> Correction to addition 3. I wrote 'keys only from M5 (persist, install, share) onward'; that mapping was mine, not settled. The legacy 'milestone 2' in CAPABILITIES is the old numbering, and principals' signing keys have no new milestone yet. Write it as: an agent holds no keys until principals' signing keys exist. Then it holds only a key its approval named, with the one message shape that key may sign. The milestone is whatever plan/ assigns principals' signing keys; if no plan page does, list it under Open on the agents page.
